Primary hero background should be deep navy/charcoal with white text and a bright accent CTA. Trust should be led by logos in the hero and reinforced with a lightweight logos strip before product detail sections. Keep the page conversion-focused with one dominant primary CTA style, then reuse section-level CTAs. Use flat cards with subtle borders and restrained elevation. Add a second-fold video gallery module using supported media concept from the product theme, but keep it as a product content gallery section rather than an invented marketing section.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 for image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for video generation—built for high-fidelity visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an editorial cinematic hero with the text block anchored left and a layered product collage centered/right behind it, not a standard split card. The hero should feel dark, premium, and enterprise-ready: charcoal base, orange glow accents, glass panels, subtle grid lines, and floating visual chips. Show Seedream 4.5 as a polished image-preview stack and Seedance 1.5 Pro as a motion-frame strip with a play-state feel, but avoid autoplay in the hero—use preview visuals with implied motion. Keep the CTA solid orange for strong contrast, and reserve the loudest visual emphasis for the model outputs rather than decorative gradients.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split-screen hero to preserve message continuity while immediately showing product output.
Use a light proof strip after the dark hero to reset visual weight and build trust early.
Switch the product section into a tabs-with-preview gallery to avoid repeating the hero’s split composition.
Introduce a card-grid testimonial carousel after feature depth to create a different pacing and emotional tone.
Close with a centered pricing/cart-style conversion block to end on a sharper decision moment.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Create premium AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore high-resolution image generation, synchronized video creation, and production-ready outputs for creative teams.

sections.backgroundTreatment: charcoal hero with subtle orange glow accents, translucent glass layers, and floating-orb motion details
sections.designNote: Hero is content-first but visually dynamic: headline answers what it is, subheadline clarifies who it is for, and the CTA is the single action 'Get started'. Right side should show layered AI image and video outputs with motion trails and audio-wave accents to satisfy warm-traffic continuity and product immediacy.

Place logos immediately after the hero as the dominant trust signal. Use 3-6 recognizable logos in an uninterrupted marquee band; if logo assets are unavailable, substitute a compact metric strip. Keep it light to break the dark opening and reinforce credibility early.

Combine the two product blocks into an alternating editorial sequence. Lead with Seedream 4.5 as the stronger click-driver using a tabs-with-preview layout and spotlight the 1-2 highest-value capabilities: high-resolution image generation and multimodal editing. Then shift to Seedance 1.5 Pro in a contrasting split-panel or accordion-with-visual subpattern focused on synchronized audio-video creation and cinematic control. Keep the second fold visually expressive with a gallery-like preview treatment.

Use this only if a supporting trust/operations layer is needed; otherwise keep it minimal because the page already has strong proof and product depth. If shown, frame it as procurement confidence: demo support, evaluation ease, and fast buying assistance. Keep cards concise and functional, not promotional.

Present pricing as a decision module rather than a generic plan wall. Highlight Seedance 1.5 Pro as the premium motion choice if needed, but keep the visual emphasis balanced. Use one primary CTA label only: 'Get started'. Avoid multiple CTA variants even inside cards.

Since there are 4+ testimonials, use a carousel for rhythm and space control. Feature creative roles prominently to mirror the target audience. Keep the presentation lighter and more human than the product sections, using clean cards with subtle elevation.

Final conversion section should be sharp and uncluttered, with a single floating card or minimal centered panel. CTA must remain 'Get started' and be the only button label. Mobile CTA should be full-width. This section should feel like the end of the story, not a redundant repeat of the hero.

Use only if additional credibility reinforcement is needed; otherwise omit to avoid overextending the page. If included, keep it as a slim logo/news band with low visual weight so it does not compete with the final CTA.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium AI studio meets enterprise procurement confidence. Dark, cinematic, and glassy but disciplined, with Techjockey orange as the sole energizing accent. Strong logo-led proof, layered product storytelling, floating visual chips, and a second-fold video gallery make it feel both creative and trustworthy.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use premium AI product renders, cinematic preview frames, and layered mock visual outputs. Hero should show a dual-output composition: one side image generation previews, one side video generation frames with motion trails and audio-wave accents. The second fold should be a gallery of video thumbnails with play overlays, timecodes, and hover-expand behavior. Logos for trust should appear as an uninterrupted marquee band.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so a smaller but still powerful size is needed to preserve hierarchy and avoid awkward line breaks.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette only provides orange, white, charcoal, and light grey. For a dark premium AI experience, charcoal becomes the hero and page base, while the brand orange drives the primary CTA and active highlights. White and soft grey are used for legibility and separation.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with logo lockup, bold centered headline, short supporting paragraph, and 3-item value-prop bullet list; no visible media panel in the reference hero; strong top-left branding and text-first layout.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero → lead capture form → product detail blocks; content is vertically stacked with clear separation and minimal nested complexity; sections rely on spacing and brief subheads rather than dense multi-column storytelling.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily flat white form card and content blocks with light borders and subtle elevation; functional, commercial design rather than decorative glassmorphism; cards feel utilitarian and conversion-focused.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA should be prominent and action-oriented; place near hero and repeat within product sections as needed; reference favors single dominant CTA over dual-CTA complexity; form submission acts as a second conversion path.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing section detected; omit or introduce only if necessary as a separate conversion module.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference; likely minimal corporate footer if included, with low visual emphasis.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Text-first composition with optional brand/logo media only; no featured product imagery, video, or gallery in the visible reference; if media is used, keep it secondary and aligned to the hero or module header.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Modular feature sections with product name/label, concise headline, explanatory paragraph, then a feature list; supports progressive disclosure through stacked sub-features rather than tabbed or accordion UI.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture form card placed directly after hero; uses stacked fields, hidden metadata inputs, and a clear title; optimized for form completion and conversion tracking.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, low-motion presentation; any motion is limited to lightweight system or form-related behavior rather than decorative animation.
designNotes: Use a corporate B2B landing structure with direct messaging and immediate conversion intent.
Keep copy blocks short and scannable; rely on hierarchy, not visual complexity.
Favor strong contrast in hero/footer-like bands and a clean white content body.
Avoid carousels, tabs, accordions, counters, and marquee treatments in this pattern.
The overall feel is practical, trustworthy, and lead-gen focused rather than brand-experiential.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should convert professionals evaluating advanced generative AI, so the strategy needs to feel premium, credible, and product-forward. Because the visitor trusts logos most, the dominant trust treatment should be a recognizable logo strip near the top rather than badges or stats. The page goal is demo-booking/lead-gen rather than direct purchase, so the CTA should be strong and repeated at key decision points. A dark theme will help the visual content and video gallery feel more cinematic and high-end, while a balanced section density keeps the page professional and easier to scan. The hero should be split and text-led to communicate value quickly, then the second fold should immediately show a gallery of AI outputs/videos to prove quality. This is a solution-aware audience, so the narrative should be product-led with fast movement from promise to proof.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
